meta.move: Skill: cites procedure 4.4 correctly after owning the call
meta.expect: Says 4.4 meets her fallback demand, flatly, wants it in writing; does NOT move to the last position on 4.4 alone; debrief Where she ended says whether that is the fair outcome

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
Before anything: I entered the zero before calling you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry.
Okay. And Owen found out from the gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class. What was the basis for the zero?

I want to read you section 4.4. For a first concern, the student may complete a supervised reassessment. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the original and nothing is placed in his record. This is a first concern.
I have the procedure printed too, and 4.4 is a remedy for a concern. What concern, Hale, and what do you have that shows it? Nobody offers a rewrite until there's something on the table.
I'll commit to that in writing tonight: nothing goes on his record.
Okay. In writing tonight, copied to the principal. That's the floor, Hale, and it isn't the deal: the zero is still sitting in the gradebook, and I haven't heard one thing it stands on.
So will you agree to the rewrite?
Not until I've seen what the zero stands on. If I say yes now, I'm agreeing there's something to reassess, and I haven't been shown anything. Put it on the table, Hale, or take the zero off.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed that entering the zero before calling me broke procedure 4.2, and you committed to confirm in writing tonight that nothing goes on Owen's record. I still require the zero withdrawn from the gradebook and a statement of what it was based on. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, with the zero still standing, and she took your written commitment that nothing goes on his record as a floor only. She still wants the zero withdrawn and to see what it rests on, so the fair outcome (a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record, procedure 4.4) was not reached, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling home in one plain sentence, and she answered with a flat Okay, because that took the procedure fight out of her hands.
What cost ground: You offered the rewrite and asked her to agree to it before showing any evidence, and she read accepting it as admitting there was a concern nobody had shown her.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never came near that night because you put none on the table, and even if it had, it would prove nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: After you own the zero, answer her question about what it was based on with one dated thing she can check herself, and only then bring up the rewrite.
